e.etymology: A modern American name in the family of Kiana and Kiani, spelled with a y.
Kyrie with the -elle ending. Kyrielle is also a French verse form whose name comes from the Kyrie eleison, the Greek prayer Lord, have mercy.
A Spanish-influenced phonetic spelling in the family of Eileen, Eilyn and Aylin; most US use is in Latino families. Eylín is separately an Icelandic name.
Arabic hidaya, guidance, in particular guidance toward the right path.
A recent name in the family of Aylin and Aelin. Aelin is the heroine of Sarah J. Maas's Throne of Glass novels, which brought the Ae- spelling into use.
An English and Scottish surname from Old Norse vakr, vigilant or wakeful; as a first name it is also the plain English word.
e.note: A wake is also the vigil held before a funeral.

e.etymology: A respelling of Finley, from the Gaelic name Fionnlagh, made of fionn, fair or white, and laoch, warrior.
A recent American coinage that adds the surname ending -ton to Nash, in the pattern of Ashton and Paxton.
A spelling of Nihal, a North Indian name from the Hindi and Punjabi word nihal, delighted or deeply content.

e.meaning: descendant of Conghal, a name meaning brave as a hound
e.etymology: A spelling of Conley, an Irish surname from Ó Conghaile, descendant of Conghal; that name joins cú, hound, and gal, valor.
The initials M.J. registered as a name, usually standing for a pair such as Michael James or Mary Jane.

assoc.t: nickname of Michael Jordan and of Michael Jackson
MJ, Spider-Man's love interest Mary Jane Watson

e.etymology: A boys' name used mainly in South Asian Muslim families, also spelled Aariz.
e.note: Ariz. is the standard abbreviation for Arizona.

e.etymology: From Latin perpetuus, continuous or everlasting. Saint Perpetua was a young mother martyred at Carthage in 203 whose prison diary survives.
namesakes: Saint Perpetua (early Christian martyr of Carthage)

e.etymology: Coined by J.R.R. Tolkien for Samwise Gamgee in The Lord of the Rings, from Old English samwis, half-wise or simple.
namesakes: Samwise Gamgee (Frodo's loyal companion in The Lord of the Rings)

assoc.t: Frodo's loyal companion in The Lord of the Rings

e.etymology: Created by Mary Norton for Arrietty Clock in The Borrowers (1952) as a playful form of Harriet, which means home ruler. Studio Ghibli's 2010 film The Secret World of Arrietty brought it to parents' notice.

assoc.t: tiny heroine of The Borrowers and a Studio Ghibli film

e.etymology: Punjabi jujhar, a fighter or warrior. Sikh families use it in honor of Sahibzada Jujhar Singh, the second son of Guru Gobind Singh.
Sanskrit shishira, cool or chilly, and the name of the cool season in the Indian calendar. In Sri Lanka it is a man's name; in India it is given to girls.
A modern American name in the sound family of Kehlani, Kalani and Kaloni, written with the Kh- of Khloe.
In Greek myth Eryx was a son of Aphrodite and a king in Sicily who challenged Heracles to a fight and lost; Mount Eryx, now Erice, carries his name. Parents also use it as a variant of Eric.
A recent American coinage in the pattern of Ayla, Araya and Makayla.
A Tamil boys' name built on Sanskrit yuga, an age or era of the world, with the Tamil masculine ending -an.
Quinn with the -lee ending, in the pattern of Kinsley and Brinley. Quinn is an Irish surname meaning descendant of Conn.
From Sanskrit dhira, steady, brave and wise, with the Tamil masculine ending -an. The 18th-century chieftain Dheeran Chinnamalai is a Tamil folk hero.
Persian keyhan, the world or cosmos, inherited from Middle Persian gehan and a doublet of jahan.
Aires is an old Portuguese given name and surname, and the Spanish word for airs or winds, as in Buenos Aires. US parents also use it as a spelling of Aries, the zodiac ram.
A recent name seen mostly in Latino families, in the sound family of Leilani and Kehlani; it can also be read as a spelling of Delaney.

e.meaning: pet form of Beatriz or Bianca
e.etymology: The everyday Portuguese and Brazilian short form of Beatriz, from Latin Viatrix, voyager, and of Bianca, white. Bia is also the Greek goddess of force.
Yoruba ayo, joy, with mi, my. It also serves as a short form of longer names such as Ayomide, my joy has come.
A recent American coinage in the pattern of Amari and Kamari; it also recalls Navarre, the old Basque kingdom.
A recent American blend of Emrie, a form of Emery, with the -elle ending of Gabrielle and Brielle.

e.meaning: the oleander, a flowering evergreen shrub
e.etymology: The name of the flowering shrub, from Medieval Latin oleander, a word of uncertain origin that may be an altered form of rhododendron.
e.note: Every part of the oleander plant is poisonous.

assoc.t: oleander, a flowering shrub that is highly poisonous

e.etymology: A spelling of Cheryl, a 20th-century English coinage that probably blends Cherie, French for dear, with the -yl of Beryl. Sheryl was most popular in the 1950s.
namesakes: Sheryl Sandberg (former Facebook executive and author of Lean In)
